title: Check numerical and performance claims in the production execution mode
applies_when: A change saves Python dispatch or launch overhead, uses a runtime override, routes on tensor shape, or infers low-precision intermediate arithmetic from Python source while production uses compilation or CUDA graph replay.
lesson: Compare baseline and candidate in the same production execution mode and verify the changed path executes there. Recheck the current baseline's implementation layer before porting old wins: replacement by native or IR operators can invalidate an old reference/performance comparison even when the custom entry still exists. Graph replay can remove the CPU work that dominated an eager experiment. Compilation can also promote low-precision intermediates or fuse away rounding boundaries: missing .float() in Python is not by itself a compiled precision defect. First run the actual decorated public entry with represented inputs and upstream gradients matched to an independently defined reference; include the native operator as a control and inspect generated arithmetic when useful. An undecorated function is a diagnostic, not a substitute for that entry. Report startup and capture separately from steady-state latency. When dispatch needs the logical phase or valid row count, verify it still receives that information under padded or compiled execution.
avoid_when: An eager diagnostic cannot establish either a graph-mode speedup or a compiled numerical regression. Missing compiled benefit does not make every eager workload irrelevant; value remains workload-specific. A compiler upcast mechanism does not prove that every operation, dtype, configuration or backend computes in FP32 or is correct. Preserve each failing dtype/reference cell instead of relaxing its tolerance or declaring the whole screen passed because the target dtype passed. Do not add graph-specific machinery to a workload that only uses eager execution.

evidence.note: At this revision GemmaRMSNorm.forward_native delegates to ir.ops.rms_norm or fused_add_rms_norm and forward_cuda delegates to it. This is current implementation-layer evidence, not proof that IR is faster or numerically equivalent to every earlier implementation. Requalify against it before transferring an old eager normalization speedup.

The old eager-only proposal was withdrawn after default-compiled path nonselection and the later IR baseline change were recognized. It preserves the earlier limited measurements rather than treating them as a current production gain; this is a scope/stop decision, not a matched current-IR performance experiment or measured Scout-efficiency result.
PyTorch documents fixed replay arguments, reduced CPU overhead and omitted CPU work during replay. Production routing and performance conclusions remain candidate-specific hypotheses.

PyTorch v2.11.0 Triton code generation explicitly promotes loaded FP16/BF16 values to FP32 when codegen_upcast_to_fp32 is enabled; triton_compute_type also documents the compute-type promotion at lines977-979. This is a configuration-dependent source mechanism, not proof of a particular generated kernel, numerical tolerance, other backend or performance gain.

FLA fast_gelu_impl calls torch.compile-decorated forward/backward functions even though their Python expressions omit explicit .float(). A low-precision eager calculation therefore does not execute the same production path. Source/caller evidence only; unpublished GPU observations and numerical values are not public qualification evidence in this card.
